authorization: User requested Orders notification debugging, lightweight reliable behavior, preserved functions, proper tests and live release.
diagnosis: Read-only production aggregate returned2, matching the two unfinished orders in the screenshot; counting SQL was correct.

Live DOM showed persistent header navigation epoch1/revisionff42789817fb1d26, while current iframe supplied epoch0/revisionab4646785f3b64f0. The global lower-epoch guard rejected the fresh controller/configuration after session reset.
Baseline browser reproduction retained old-scope and made no new status request after a same-page lower-epoch remount.
Bell notifications were activity-only; no persistent unfinished-order reminder existed. Sidebar observer missed badge-only removal and did not reconnect when its observed section was replaced.

Live rollout verification identified an additional inherited pending-read cache issue: a remount could reuse an unconfirmed attempt and wait a full polling interval before obtaining its first count. Reproduced on the released baseline and covered by an interrupted-initial-read browser regression.
changes: Accept a reset epoch only for the settled current document route, with no pending navigation; retain the browser's monotonic epoch. Other-route and pending late responses remain rejected.
Restore cached badge presentation after badge/button/sidebar redraws without an additional request.
One managed timer/request per controller; thirty-second visible-page polling and rate-bounded focus/bell recovery. Shared server aggregate cache reduced from thirty to ten seconds.
Reuse the same permission-scoped count for sidebar, bell count and persistent Orders reminder. Activity stays lazy; no extra full Orders/Shopify reads.

Keep last-known counts with delayed labeling during outages; unknown is not presented as zero. Refresh open reminders on successful count changes and outages. Destroyed controllers cannot mark replacement status stale.

Only completed responses enter the status cache: interrupted initial reads restart immediately on remount, while completed failures retain bounded backoff and explicit unavailable state. Never render an undefined count.
